1.note: Read as בְּדוֹלַח, bdellium or crystal (Gen 2:12, Num 11:7), as in line 57 בְּדֹלָחֶיהָ וְדָרֶיהָ "its crystals and its pearls". The pointing here is unusual.

2.note: The Cutheans (2 Kgs 17:24) are the Samaritans. The Hebrew rhymes כּוּתִים (Kutim) with כְּרוּתִים (kerutim, "cut off").

3.note: The edition prints these words in square brackets. "To reveal aspects in the Torah" is the rabbinic phrase for interpreting it against the halakha (m. Avot 3:11).

4.note: Lev 22:23 שָׂרוּעַ וְקָלוּט: an animal with a limb too long or too short (stunted). Here the sense is that the sect is small and has not grown.

5.note: מִינִים means "kinds" and also "heretics", the word used for the Karaites in this gate.

6.note: The subject of "he will entice" is not named; it may be the Baal of the next line (1 Kgs 18:21), that is, the founder of the sect.

7.note: מִשְׁנֵהוּ is "his second", the king's viceroy (Esth 10:3); the word also suggests the Mishnah (מִשְׁנָה), which stands second to the Torah.

8.note: חֲמֻשִׁים is "in battle array" (Exod 13:18). Taken with the military image, the details are ranged under the general rules. A reading "fifty" is less likely.

9.note: "Drawn" (literally "trodden, bent", said of a bow in Isa 21:15). Probably the punishments of the Law; the sense is uncertain.

10.note: The Karaites forbade any light on the Sabbath, even a lamp lit before it; the Rabbanites allow a lamp lit on Friday. Job 29:3 "by his light I walked through darkness" is turned to mockery: their lamps lead them into darkness.

11.he: וּבִמְצוֹא הַחֲכָמִים נִיב מְבַטֵּל / לְנִיב אַחֵר יְבִינוּן מַעֲנֵהוּ
11.note: Read as: when one verse seems to cancel another, the sages see how to reconcile them. The construction is uncertain.

12.note: סקל is to clear of stones (Isa 62:10). חֲזֹר חֲלִילָה is a rabbinic idiom for going round again in a circle; here "turn back".

13.he: וְאִם תִּהְיֶה עֲמֻקָּה אוֹ סְמוּכָה / וְאִם תִּהְיֶה רְבוּעָה אוֹ עֲגֻלָּה
13.note: Laws of the sukkah in m. Sukkah 1 and b. Sukkah 7b–8a: a roof too high or too low, a booth resting on something else, a round booth. Which laws "deep" and "leaning" mean is uncertain.

14.note: Probably the Sabbath limit (teḥum), the distance one may walk out of town on the Sabbath. "Carryings out" (יְצִיאוֹת) are the forms of carrying from one domain to another (m. Shabbat 1:1).

15.note: The teller is Ḥever, who told the story of the debate in answer to the company's question (block 5). The frame is not closed: Heman does not speak again.
